newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mixed ahead of first notice.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mixed ahead of first notice.

text.p: CBOT soy products ended mixed on Tuesday in quiet, spread-dominated trade ahead of first notice day, traders said.

Nearby soymeal contracts were boosted by ideas there would be no deliveries posted against the May. While the cash market has slipped in recent weeks, most locations continue to bid at a premium to CBOT May making it less attractive to deliver soymeal, traders noted. First notice day is Wednesday.
Most of the soymeal spread activity was centered on the May/July spread. Trade sources said much of the action on Tuesday was nullifying positions ahead of expiry.
But some sources speculated traders were willing to take ownership of the May going into the delivery period since it was unlikely there would be many deliveries posted.

May soyoil struggled with the opposite scenario. Low demand and low cash prices, coupled with a heavy crush pace have created large soyoil stockpiles. The cash basis was quoted at 0.75 cent per lb below May futures, making it profitable to deliver against the May, traders said.
Soymeal ended $1.40 per ton higher to $0.80 lower with May up $1.40 at $283.70. Soyoil closed 0.07 cent per lb lower to 0.06 cent higher with May down 0.07 at 24.79.
On the day, Merrill Lynch and Tenco Inc each bought 150 lots July soymeal while Prudential Securities sold 300 August, pit sources said.

In spread trade, Smith Barney spread 600 lots May/July at $5.00 to $5.20, premium May, Continental Grain spread 400 lots May/July at $4.90 to $5.30 and Cargill Investor Services spread 300 May/July at $5.00 to $5.30.
In soyoil, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 300 lots July outright and Cargill sold 500 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, against Monday's 33,578 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, compared with Monday's 23,622.
